judgements.why: Sections 1-2 provide the short title, extent, and interpretation clauses (Section 2 definitions) that are the vocabulary for every answer; exam questions routinely test definition recall and application.
Sections 3-9 are the mechanics of offer and acceptance — a staple problem question and short-note topic in every semester exam.

judgements.concept: Essential Elements of a Valid Contract
judgements.why: Section 10 is the gateway provision; every exam requires stating and explaining 'all agreements are contracts if...' with its ingredients.
Sections 11-12 (minor, unsound mind, disqualified persons) are high-yield: minority agreements, ratification, and estoppel are tested every year.
Section 15 with Section 19 (voidable at option) is a standard problem-fact pattern involving threat or detention of property.
Section 16 (presumed relationships, burden of proof) plus Section 19A (set aside or set aside on terms) is a favourite essay and problem topic.
Section 17 read with Section 19 (voidable, silence not fraud unless duty to speak) is examinable both as short note and application.
Sections 18-19 (innocent misrepresentation, remedy of rescission/damages) are distinct from fraud and tested for differentiation.
Sections 20-22 (bilateral/unilateral mistake of fact vs law, identity vs quality) are a classic exam area for void vs voidable distinction.
Sections 23-25 define lawful consideration/object and exceptions (natural love, past voluntary service, time-barred debt) — direct short-note and application material.

judgements.concept: Void Agreements — Restraint of Marriage, Trade, Legal Proceedings
judgements.why: Sections 26-28 are per se void categories; reasonable restraint exceptions (sale of goodwill, partnership) are standard exam questions.
Sections 29-30 (uncertainty, wagering exception for horse-race prizes) are short-note staples and appear in MCQs.
Sections 31-36 (condition precedent/subsequent, future uncertain event) are a distinct chapter tested via problem questions on insurance-type facts.
Sections 37-67 (tender, reciprocal promises, time/place, appropriation, novation/rescission/alteration) form the largest operative chapter — heavy application problems every exam.
Sections 73-75 (compensation, remoteness Hadley v Baxendale, specific performance/injunction under Specific Relief Act cross-reference) are the remedies climax of the syllabus.
Sections 68-72 (necessaries, reimbursement, non-gratuitous act, finder of goods, mistake/coercion) are a self-contained chapter with direct problem questions.
Sections 124-125 (definition, indemnity-holder's rights) are short but tested for distinction from guarantee and for rights enumeration.
Sections 126-147 (continuing guarantee, consideration, surety's liability co-extensive) are a major special-contract chapter with multi-part problems.
Sections 133-147 (variance, release, composition, creditor's act impairing remedy, set-off) are the most heavily tested sub-topic within guarantee.
Sections 148-171 (gratuitous/non-gratuitous, standard of care, unauthorized use, mixture, termination, finder of goods) are a full problem-question chapter.
Sections 172-181 (pledge by non-owner, pawnee's rights, lien — particular/general) are tested both as short notes and in secured-transaction problems.
Sections 182-210 (express/implied, ostensible, ratification, emergency authority) are the foundation of the longest chapter; creation and scope of authority are exam constants.
Sections 211-238 (sub-agent, substituted agent, ratification requisites, termination by act/operation of law, irrevocable agency) complete the agency chapter and are heavily tested.

sequence: Contract Formation: Offer, Acceptance & Essential Elements
Legality of Object & Consideration, and Void Agreements
output.why: Follows the Act's logical architecture: formation prerequisites first, then vitiating factors that attack formation, then legality filters, then special contract types (contingent), then the operative life of a contract (performance, discharge, remedies), then statutory obligations (quasi-contracts), and finally the three named special contracts (indemnity/guarantee, bailment/pledge, agency) which build on the general principles.

exclusions.consequence: Exam answers will state rules correctly but lack illustrative authority, losing marks for 'application' and 'analysis' bands in essay questions and reducing persuasiveness in problem answers.
exclusions.when_to_learn: During revision, after mastering the bare sections; prioritize leading cases (e.g., Carlill, Hadley v Baxendale, Mohori Bibee, Satyabrata Ghose) for each chapter.

exclusions.topic: Interplay with Specific Relief Act, 1963 (specific performance, injunction, rescission)
exclusions.consequence: Remedies answers under Section 73-75 will be incomplete; the court's discretionary remedies and bars to specific performance are frequently tested alongside damages.
exclusions.when_to_learn: Alongside Module 5 (Performance, Discharge & Remedies) or in a dedicated remedies seminar.

exclusions.topic: Electronic contracts and Information Technology Act, 2000 amendments (Sections 10A, 4, 10, 11 ITA)
exclusions.consequence: Cannot address modern formation issues (clickwrap, email acceptance, automated systems) that appear in contemporary problem questions.
exclusions.when_to_learn: After Module 1, when studying communication and acceptance; or in a specialised e-commerce law course.

exclusions.topic: Government contracts and Article 299 Constitution of India
exclusions.consequence: Will miss the distinct formalities and immunity issues that arise when the State is a party — a common separate question in semester papers.
exclusions.when_to_learn: In administrative law or a dedicated government contracts module.

modules.title: Contract Formation: Offer, Acceptance & Essential Elements
covers: Essential Elements of a Valid Contract
modules.why_here: These four concepts constitute the complete formation pipeline: vocabulary, offer/acceptance mechanics, the Section 10 checklist, and capacity gatekeepers. They are taught and tested together as 'whether a valid contract exists'.
modules.capability: Analyse a fact pattern to determine whether a valid contract has been formed, identifying offer, acceptance, consideration, intention, and capacity, and stating the effect of any defect.

modules.title: Vitiating Factors: Free Consent
modules.why_here: All five vitiating factors attack the 'free consent' requirement of Section 10 and share the same remedial structure (voidable vs void). They are examined together for differentiation and remedy selection.
modules.capability: Diagnose whether consent is vitiated in a given scenario, distinguish between coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, and mistake, and state the resulting remedy (void/voidable) with the applicable section.

modules.title: Legality of Object & Consideration, and Void Agreements
covers: Void Agreements — Restraint of Marriage, Trade, Legal Proceedings
modules.why_here: Sections 23-30 form a coherent legitimacy filter: lawful consideration/object, then three categories of agreements declared void ab initio. They are tested as a block for 'is this agreement enforceable?'.
modules.capability: Evaluate whether consideration and object are lawful under Sections 23-25, and determine if an agreement falls within a statutorily void category (restraint, uncertainty, wagering), citing the relevant section and exception.

modules.title: Contingent Contracts
modules.why_here: A self-contained chapter (Sections 31-36) with a distinct logic (condition precedent/subsequent, future uncertain event) that is separately examined via insurance-type problems.
modules.capability: Apply Sections 31-36 to determine the enforceability of contingent contracts based on the happening or non-happening of future uncertain events, and distinguish contingent contracts from wagering agreements.

modules.title: Performance, Discharge & Remedies
modules.why_here: Performance (Sections 37-67) and its failure (Sections 73-75) are the operative life of a contract. Discharge modes and remedies are the practical climax of the syllabus and are always tested together.
modules.capability: Trace the performance obligations of parties under a contract, identify modes of discharge (performance, breach, agreement, frustration), and calculate remedies for breach including compensation under Hadley v Baxendale and the availability of specific relief.

modules.title: Quasi-Contracts (Relations Resembling Contract)
modules.why_here: Sections 68-72 form a standalone statutory obligation chapter with five distinct claims. It is examined independently and does not depend on the special contracts that follow.
modules.capability: Identify quasi-contractual obligations under Sections 68-72 and articulate the claim arising from necessaries supplied to incapable persons, reimbursement of interested parties, non-gratuitous acts, finder of goods, or money paid by mistake/coercion.

modules.title: Indemnity & Guarantee
modules.why_here: Indemnity (Sections 124-125) and guarantee (Sections 126-147) are taught as a pair because they are constantly distinguished. The surety's rights and discharge (Sections 133-147) are the most heavily tested part of guarantee and belong in the same module.
modules.capability: Distinguish indemnity from guarantee, explain the surety's liability (co-extensive with principal debtor) and rights (subrogation, indemnity, securities), and determine when a surety is discharged under Sections 133-147.

modules.title: Bailment & Pledge
modules.why_here: Bailment (Sections 148-171) and its species pledge (Sections 172-181) form a continuous chapter on possession-based obligations. Pledge rights and lien are tested both as short notes and in secured-transaction problems.
modules.capability: Analyse bailment and pledge scenarios to determine the duties, rights, and liabilities of bailor/bailee and pawnor/pawnee, including the standard of care, unauthorized use, mixture, termination, pawnee's sale rights, and particular vs general lien.

modules.title: Agency
modules.why_here: The longest chapter (Sections 182-238) splits naturally into creation/authority and the consequences of authority (sub-agents, ratification, termination). Both halves are required to answer any agency problem completely.
modules.capability: Determine the creation and scope of agency authority (express, implied, ostensible, emergency), the effect of ratification, the position of sub-agents vs substituted agents, and the modes of termination of agency (by act of parties or operation of law), including irrevocable agency.
